subject: Renewal: Echelon scale + pricing stability request
summary: Customer requests a 12-month price hold while increasing committed usage. Internal discussion balances discount depth, one-time credits, and acceptance window. Final proposal: 15% discount on committed baseline for 12 months if amendment signed by 2028-07-31 plus onboarding and burst credits; customer to route PO via procurement.
messages:
From: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@echelonlogistics.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@echelonlogistics.com
Date: 2028-06-28T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal: Scale + pricing stability request

Hi Priya,

Hope you9re well. Echelon is planning to double our API usage over the next 12 months as we roll LLM features into three new products. We9re preparing our budget and procurement asks, and we need two things from Redwood to get internal approval:

1) A pricing stability window (price hold) for 12 months so our finance team can forecast without churn.
2) A one-time set of onboarding/burst credits tied to the initial three months of scale — we9ll likely spike while migrating models.

We9re open to a committed baseline for predictable pricing; our initial ask is a 20% discount on current effective rates if a 12-month hold is available. If that9s not feasible, please propose alternatives (shorter hold, credit mixes, or phased commit).

I attached our Q2 usage export to give context (Echelon-usage-q2.csv). Procurement (procurement@echelonlogistics.com) will own the PO once we align terms.

Thanks,
Alex Mercer
Head of Product, Echelon Logistics
alex.mercer@echelonlogistics.com

From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@echelonlogistics.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-28T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal: Scale + pricing stability request

Hi Alex,

Thanks for the clear ask and the usage file — that helps a lot. Congrats on the product launches. We9re excited to support the scale.

Quick read: doubling usage is realistic to support, but to offer a 12-month price hold at material discount we9ll need some form of committed baseline (monthly or annual) so the economics work on our side.

Suggested next steps:
- Draft a short mutual action plan (MAP) that captures baseline commit, burst credits, timing, and the sign-by date. I9ve attached a MAP draft for discussion (MAP-draft.pdf).
- Internally I9ll run this with pricing and deals to surface options (6-month vs 12-month hold, discount tiers tied to committed qps/TU).

A few immediate options I9ll circulate internally: 12-month price hold with 125 discount on committed baseline (+ onboarding credits), or 6-month hold with 185 discount plus larger one-time credits. I9ll follow up with a short internal thread and come back with a proposed amendment.

Can you confirm Echelon9s preferred sign-by date? If you can aim for July 31 that gives us a clean window for Q3 provisioning.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
priya@redwood.ai

From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.ai>
To: ben_carter <ben@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, david_kim <david@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-29T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Renewal: Scale + pricing stability request — quick pricing ask

Folks, forwarding Echelon9s request. Key points: they want a 12-month price hold + ~2x usage. They9re open to commit. My suggested constructs below, need guidance on permissible discount and credit sizing so we can respond with a clean MAP.

Options I9m proposing for EM (customer):
A) 12-month price hold, 12% discount on committed baseline (commit = current Q2 run-rate * 1.8), plus 1.5 months onboarding credits (token credits) to cover migration spikes. Sign-by: 2028-07-31.
B) 6-month price hold, 18% discount on committed baseline, larger onboarding credit (3 months), and a usage true-up at month 7.
C) No price hold, but a tiered commit with step-up discounts as they hit bands (conservative discount now, bigger discounts after 6 months).

Questions: what9s the max discount we can approve without legal exec sign-off? Also, can we offer a one-time "burst credit" equal to ~10% of estimated 3-month spike? Finally, any constraints on DocuSign turnaround or procurement PO timing we should flag?

Thanks,
Priya

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: priya_natarajan <priya@redwood.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-29T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Renewal: Scale + pricing stability request — quick pricing ask

Priya,

We can authorize up to a 15% standard discount for renewals from AE level. Anything beyond that needs revenue ops sign-off. I9d prefer Option A as our baseline offer: 12% for 12 months + onboarding credits. But to close quickly, I9d trade to 15% discount if they sign a firm 12-month commit (1.8x Q2 run-rate) by 2028-07-31. Also ok to include a one-time burst credit equal to 8% of estimated Q2 run if it helps bridge spikes.

If they accept 15% we can fast-track amendment and pre-approve the DocuSign template. I9ve attached the internal pricing grid I9m thinking of (pricing-grid.xlsx).

-Ben
VP Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@echelonlogistics.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-07-01T15:22:00-07:00
Subject: Proposal: renewal amendment + stability window (Echelon Logistics)

Alex,

Thanks for the patience while we worked this through. Based on internal approvals here9s a clear proposal to put in an amendment: 

1) Price stability: 12-month price hold from the amendment effective date.
2) Discount: 15% off your committed baseline charges (committed baseline = current Q2 run-rate * 1.8). Discount applies only to committed baseline tokens.
3) Onboarding credits: one-time credit equal to 8% of Q2 spend, applied to the first billing cycle after provisioning.
4) Burst/Spike protection: additional token credit pool to cover estimated migration spikes for first 90 days (detailed sizing in the amendment).
5) Sign-by: 2028-07-31 to lock 15% and the credits.

I attached the proposed amendment (Echelon-renewal-amendment-v1.docx) and a DocuSign link to sign once you9re ready (https://www.docusign.com/en/sign/abc123-echelon-renewal). We believe this balances Echelon9s need for predictability and our need for a committed baseline to underwrite the price hold.

If procurement needs anything else (PO language, invoicing cadence), loop them in or send the contact and we9ll coordinate with finance.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
priya@redwood.ai

From: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@echelonlogistics.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@echelonlogistics.com
Date: 2028-07-02T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: renewal amendment + stability window (Echelon Logistics)

Priya,

Thanks — this looks reasonable and in line with what finance was hoping for. We9ll route the amendment through procurement. Please hold the 15% and the credits until 2028-07-31 as requested. Our procurement contact, Mira Shah (procurement@echelonlogistics.com), will manage the PO and sign-off.

Two quick asks from procurement: can Redwood include standard language stating that onboarding credits cannot be reallocated beyond the first billing cycle, and can you provide an invoice template for the committed baseline? If you can drop those into the DocuSign package that would speed things.

I9ll circle back with the PO number when procurement issues it.

Appreciate the fast turnaround.
Alex
Head of Product, Echelon Logistics
